trial.title: Identification of the Mechanism of Non-histaminergic Itch Inducing Epigenetic Changes

endpoints.measure: Assessment of itch: visual analog scale (VAS)
endpoints.description: Itch following pruritogens will be monitored for 15 minutes using a computerized 100 mm visual analog scale (eVAS software Aalborg University, Denmark), installed on a tablet. The scale range from 0 (no itch) to 100 (worst imaginable itch).

endpoints.measure: Assessment of pain: visual analog scale (VAS)
endpoints.description: Pain following pruritogen will be monitored for 15 minutes using a computerized 100 mm visual analog scale (eVAS software Aalborg University, Denmark), installed on a tablet. The scale range from 0 (no pain) to 100 (worst imaginable pain).

analysis_trace.content: NCT06997926 is a basic science interventional study investigating non-histaminergic itch mechanisms using cowhage spicules. The trial employs a parallel randomized design with active cowhage vs inactive cowhage (sham) in 30 healthy adults aged 18-60. Primary endpoints focus on plasma miRNA and protein expression changes over time; secondary endpoints measure itch and pain intensity via VAS.

Healthy volunteers (n=30), ages 18-60, English-speaking, excluding pregnancy, drug addiction, neurological/immunological disorders, skin diseases, or medications affecting itch. This is a convenience sample of healthy adults, not patients with chronic pruritus.

Cowhage contains mucunain, a cysteine protease that activates PAR-2 receptors and Mrgpr receptors (MRGPRX1, MRGPRX2), inducing histamine-independent itch via polymodal C-fibers. Evidence from Papoiu et al. (2011) and Reddy et al. (2017) confirms cowhage produces intense, prolonged itch distinct from histamine pathway.

Primary endpoints (primary-0 to primary-7): Exploratory biomarker endpoints measuring miRNA and protein expression at baseline, 30min, 3h, 24h. No predefined success threshold; study is hypothesis-generating. Secondary endpoints (secondary-0, secondary-1): VAS measurements of itch and pain (0-100mm) immediately post-application, assessed over 15 minutes.

Direct evidence: Cowhage reliably induces itch in healthy volunteers (Papoiu et al. 2011: mean VAS ~40-60mm, peak higher than histamine). Mechanism studies (Reddy et al. 2017) confirm Mrgpr activation. No direct evidence for miRNA/protein changes specific to this protocol. Evidence role: direct_numeric for VAS itch magnitude (indirect, from similar studies); mechanism_background for miRNA/protein (no numeric anchors).

No published results from this specific trial. No direct evidence linking cowhage exposure to specific plasma miRNA or protein expression changes. Epigenetic biomarker response magnitude and time course are unknown. Trial is basic science with exploratory endpoints.

Cowhage application is generally safe in healthy volunteers. Expected adverse events: transient localized itch, burning, pricking sensations. No serious risks anticipated with cutaneous spicule application in healthy skin. No systemic safety concerns expected from blood sampling (20mL total).

1) High variability in biomarker response may limit signal detection in n=15 per group. 2) miRNA/protein changes may be subtle and require sensitive assays. 3) 24h timepoint may show return to baseline for most biomarkers. 4) Sham control (inactive cowhage) should produce minimal itch, serving as valid comparator.
